newsitem.title: USA: April production steady, slowed by strikes.
newsitem.headline: April production steady, slowed by strikes.

text.p: Production by the nation's mines, factories and utilities was flat in April for the first time since last summer as strikes and related plant shutdowns slowed auto output, the Federal Reserve said on Thursday.

Industrial production was unchanged last month after climbing a smaller-than-previously estimated 0.6 percent in March, the Fed said. It was the weakest showing for the industrial sector since last July, when output also was flat.

The capacity use rate, which measures how near to production limits businesses are operating, retreated to a somewhat less intense 83.4 percent from a smaller-than-previously reported 83.7 percent in March, which was still the highest rate since September 1995.
The performance of the industrial sector, which has been operating vigorously for several months, was weaker than the 0.2 percent rise Wall Street economists had expected.
Indications of a slowing industrial sector could influence Federal Reserve policy-makers, who are scheduled to meet next week to decide whether to raise interest rates.
The central bank increased short-term rates by a quarter point in March, seeking to cool demand and check potential inflationary pressures by raising the cost of borrowing.
Strikes and related plant shutdowns at General Motors Corp. and Chrysler Corp. contributed to last month's lack of growth in the overall industrial sector, the Fed said.
The work stoppages accounted for more than half of the 6.8 percent drop in motor vehicle output last month, which followed a scant 0.1 percent rise in March.
As a result, motor vehicle assemblies fell in April to a rate of 5.7 million a year for cars from 6.2 million in March and light truck assemblies fell to 5.2 million from 6 million.
Excluding motor vehicles and parts, overall industrial output rose 0.3 percent last month after a 0.6 percent increase in March.
Broken down by sector, the Fed said factory output fell 0.2 percent in April after rising 0.5 percent a month earlier.
Production by mining industries fell 0.5 percent in April after a 0.9 percent gain in March.
Electric and gas utilities, reacting to relatively cool temperatures, boosted their output 2 percent last month following a 0.9 percent rise in March.
